content: 1. Both clarithromycin and other QTc-prolonging drugs can increase the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications to mitigate the risk of arrhythmias. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, which raises the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely if coadministered. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 5. Clarithromycin and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval, making their coadministration contraindicated due to the risk of severe cardiac arrhythmias. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage as needed. 7. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of ifosfamide. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Clarithromycin and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone also increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely if coadministered. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Both clarithromycin and imipramine prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels of indacaterol (inhaled) by modulating P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor closely. No dose adjustment is warranted at the 75 mcg dose. 12. Clarithromycin and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval, making their coadministration contraindicated. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Isoniazid increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased calcium channel blocker effects may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. 18. Clarithromycin and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ketamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 32. Lenacapavir increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Clarithromycin and levalbuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Clarithromycin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 42. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor closely. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 43. Clarithromycin and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Clarithromycin and lofexidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Clarithromycin increases lomitapide levels several-fold by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 48. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
